ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at one value at a time and gives it its sort key; hops 1-3 pass the pair on (each documented as ordering by sort keys) and hop 4 compares the two keys it is given (lower key first, the same key gives 0, as its javadoc states). Once negative values receive their raw bit patterns as keys, their order is reversed, and a hop above can only restore it by ordering the pair without the keys. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc lists the order largest to smallest (normal negative numbers above -MAX_VALUE above negative infinity); the double overload of compare orders negative doubles by value (testCompareDouble passes); the deprecated org.apache.commons.lang.NumberUtils.compare(float, float) orders negative floats the same way (its testCompareFloat passes); CompareToBuilder.append(float, float) is a production caller of the facade (testFloat passes), and MutableFloat.compareTo is a second production caller (testCompareTo passes).
